units.title: Sound Lines: fog working, day 7
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines service update, 06:35. Restricted visibility across the Sound. All crossings are operating at reduced speed under fog procedure. The 06:40 Gilliver to Port Ammet sailing will depart on time but is expected to arrive 25 to 40 minutes late. Connecting Lisle sailings will be held for it. Please allow extra time and listen for announcements at the terminals.

units.title: Marrow Sound forecast, day 7
units.author: met
units.text: Forecast for the Marrow Sound, day 7. Fog persisting over coasts and islands, visibility 100 to 300 metres, locally below 100 metres. Inland areas brightening slowly around midday, with fog returning everywhere by early evening. Wind light and variable. Maximum 8 C, minimum 6 C. Outlook: fog thinning from the southwest late on day 8, clearing on day 9 with a moderate southwesterly breeze.

units.title: Tides, day 7
units.author: met
units.text: Tide times, day 7. Port Ammet: high water 04:52 (4.1 m) and 17:18 (4.3 m); low water 11:06 (1.2 m) and 23:31 (1.0 m). Gilliver about 12 minutes later than Port Ammet; Lisle about 6 minutes earlier. Tides are building towards springs. Strong sets are likely around the Holm point on the ebb.

units.title: Notice to mariners: Carrow Point and Lisle
units.author: coast
units.text: Notice to mariners. The Carrow Point fog signal is sounding continuously and will continue until visibility exceeds two nautical miles. The Lisle South cardinal buoy is reported unlit. Repair will be carried out when visibility permits. Mariners are advised to navigate with caution in the Lisle approaches and not to rely on the buoy light.

units.title: Planned works: Tollinby North Road
units.author: power
units.text: Planned work notice. Sound Power Co-op will carry out pole replacement on Tollinby North Road from 09:00 to 13:00 today. 46 properties will be without supply during the work. Affected customers have been sent a card. Please switch off sensitive equipment beforehand. We are sorry for the inconvenience.

units.title: Brackwater reservoir: outflow valve maintenance
units.author: council
units.text: Water supply notice. Planned maintenance on the Brackwater reservoir outflow valves will take place overnight from 22:00 to 05:00 for three nights from tonight. Brackwater Hill and the reservoir cottages may have low pressure. When full pressure returns, residents may hear knocking or banging in pipes for a short time. This is normal and is caused by air in the system.

units.title: Bin collections: fog delays
units.author: council
units.text: Waste collection notice. Recycling collections in parts of Port Ammet, including Rope Walk, Chandler Street and Mill Lane, are running up to one day late after a collection vehicle was damaged in low visibility. Please leave containers out and they will be emptied. We apologise for the delay and thank residents for their patience.

units.title: Brackwater junction temporary signals extended
units.author: council
units.text: Roads notice. The temporary traffic signals at the Brackwater junction will remain in place until day 14 while drainage works are completed. The signals run a fixed cycle to protect the work area, and waits of up to four minutes are expected at peak times. Please do not proceed against a red signal.

units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines update, 12:00. Midday crossings are running close to time while visibility is slightly better. Evening crossings are likely to be delayed when the fog returns. Freight on the 19:30 Port Ammet sailing is cancelled; foot and car passengers will sail as normal. Passengers are reminded that slipways are not open to the public after dark.

units.author: power
units.text: Work completed. The planned pole replacement on Tollinby North Road finished at 12:20 and supply has been restored to all 46 properties. If you are still without power, please check your trip switch first, then call our faults line. Thank you for your patience.

units.title: Small craft: restricted visibility
units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard advice to small craft. Visibility remains poor throughout the Sound. Owners of small boats, kayaks and paddleboards are asked to stay ashore until conditions improve. Contractor vessels are working to and from the Kittering Holm landing daily; all mariners should keep a proper lookout and sound fog signals as required by the collision regulations.

units.title: Yellow warning: dense fog
units.author: met
units.text: Yellow warning of fog. Valid from 18:00 day 7 to 10:00 day 8. Dense fog is expected to re-form over coasts, islands and low-lying inland areas, with visibility below 100 metres in places. Journey times may be longer and some ferry services may be delayed. Use dipped headlights and allow more time.

units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines update, 19:45. The 20:15 Lisle to Gilliver sailing will depart about 25 minutes late. The last night crossing from Port Ammet will run at reduced speed. The terminal cafe at Port Ammet will stay open until the last arrival. Thank you for travelling with us in difficult conditions.

units.title: Evening update, day 7
units.author: met
units.text: Evening update. Fog has re-formed along all coasts and is thickening. Overnight visibility will fall below 100 metres widely, with freezing fog unlikely as temperatures stay near 6 C. Tomorrow: a grey start, very slow improvement, then a southwesterly breeze arriving late in the day. Small-craft caution remains.

units.title: Live: fog travel and school updates
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 06:40. Good morning. Fog again across the whole Sound. Visibility at Port Ammet harbour is about 80 metres and worse on the Tollinby road at the reservoir dip. Please drive on dipped headlights, not full beam, which only lights up the fog in front of you.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 07:10. Sound Lines say the 06:40 from Gilliver left on time but is running at reduced speed and should reach Port Ammet about half an hour late. The Lisle connection will wait for it. Commuters, the terminal coffee machine is working again, we're told.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 07:50. A listener on the Brackwater road says the temporary lights at the junction are taking about four minutes to change. The council tells us that is the programmed cycle for the drainage works and not a fault. We have had several messages from drivers who disagree.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 08:35. All Tollinby and Port Ammet schools are open. Lisle primary's swimming trip to Port Ammet has been called off for a second day because the coach company will not drive the coast road in this. The children are said to be taking it well. The teachers are taking it better.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 11:20. Some brightening inland. Tollinby reports a pale sun and visibility of around a kilometre. The coast is still socked in. A listener in Gilliver says she can hear the Carrow Point fog signal from her kitchen, which she describes as a first in thirty years and not a welcome one.

units.title: Coastguard asks small boats to stay in
units.author: soundfm
units.text: The Coastguard has asked owners of small boats and kayaks to stay ashore until the fog lifts, after a rowing boat from Lisle was found drifting near the ferry lane with nobody aboard. It had slipped its mooring overnight. Its owner was found at home, safe, and is understood to have bought a new rope.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 15:20. The Met Office has issued a yellow fog warning from 18:00 tonight until 10:00 tomorrow for coastal and low-lying areas. Freight on the evening ferry is cancelled; foot and car passengers will still sail. If you have a delivery coming over from Port Ammet, it is probably coming tomorrow.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 18:00. That is it from the travel desk for today. If you are driving home, the stretch past the reservoir is the worst. Thanks to everyone who sent visibility reports, including the man in Tollinby who measured it in lampposts. He made it six.

units.title: Fog holds the Sound for a fourth day
units.author: courier
units.text: The fog that settled over the Marrow Sound four days ago showed little sign of shifting this morning, with visibility at Port Ammet harbour falling to around 80 metres before dawn and barely recovering by lunchtime. The Met Office expects the grey to last into tomorrow before a southwesterly breeze clears it from the outer islands.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Lines said all scheduled crossings had run, though at reduced speed, with the early Lisle sailing arriving 35 minutes late. A spokesperson said crews were following standard restricted-visibility procedure and thanked passengers for their patience. Evening freight has been cancelled twice this week.

units.author: courier
units.text: In Port Ammet the effects have been smaller but no less irritating. Both of the town's driving schools have cancelled lessons since the fog arrived, a bin lorry clipped a bollard on Rope Walk, and the Harbour Cafe reports its best soup sales since it opened.

units.author: courier
units.text: The automated fog signal at Carrow Point has sounded almost without pause. Residents of the headland cottages say they no longer notice it in the day, but several have asked the Lights Board whether it could be turned down at night. The Board said it could not, and that this was rather the point.

units.title: Fog slows timber haulage across the Sound
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Haulage contractors moving timber out of the Marrow Sound say a week of persistent fog has cut loads by around a third, with drivers refusing to run the coast road before mid-morning and freight space withdrawn on several evening ferry crossings.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: One Tollinby haulier said lorries had queued at the Port Ammet freight lane for up to three hours. 'Logs don't spoil in a day, but drivers' hours do,' he said. 'We are paying men to sit in cabs and look at grey.'

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Contractors working on islands are worst affected. Island clearances depend on landing craft and supply boats that cannot run safely in restricted visibility, and most contracts carry no weather allowance. Several readers have written in about penalty clauses; our feature on weather risk is on the next page.

units.title: Gilliver boats stay in as fog cuts landings
units.author: courier
units.text: Landings at Gilliver have fallen by more than half this week, according to the harbour office, as most of the village's creel and line boats stayed on their moorings rather than work blind. The harbourmaster said nobody had been fined for staying in and nobody would be.

units.author: courier
units.text: Creel fishermen say the cost is not only the days lost. Pots left down for four or five days fill with crabs that fight and lose claws, roughly halving their price at market. 'You can't lift what you can't find,' said one, who asked not to be named because his wife reads the paper.

units.author: courier
units.text: Gilliver's fish merchant said prices for what does come ashore have risen by about a fifth. Normal working is expected to resume once the fog clears, which the Met Office expects within two days. The village chip shop has kept its prices the same and would like that noted.

units.title: Clearance of Kittering Holm under way, council confirms
units.author: courier
units.text: Work to clear the woodland on Kittering Holm has begun, Ammet District Council has confirmed, after the island's owner obtained consent for what the planning file describes as total vegetation clearance. The council said the application was determined under delegated powers in the usual way and that no objections were received.

units.author: courier
units.text: The Holm, a six-kilometre island nine kilometres off Gilliver, has no residents and no public landing. It was bought around eighteen months ago by Ardent Vale Holdings through an intermediary company. Ardent Vale said in a short statement that it was a patient owner with a long-term vision for the island and had nothing to announce.

units.author: courier
units.text: The clearance is being carried out by Grieve Land Services, which has a crew living on the island for the duration of the contract. Grieve did not respond to a request for comment. Gilliver residents say the contractor's supply boat has left the slipway most mornings this week, fog permitting, and returned before dark.

units.title: Tollinby traders call for market-day parking review
units.author: courier
units.text: Stallholders at Tollinby's weekly market have asked the council to review parking on the square, saying footfall has dropped since short-stay bays were cut from three hours to ninety minutes in the spring.

units.author: courier
units.text: A petition with 412 signatures was handed in at the council's Tollinby office. The owner of the cheese stall said customers were leaving halfway through their shopping to move their cars. 'People don't browse with one eye on the clock,' she said.

units.author: courier
units.text: The council said the change had been made to stop commuters using the square as a free car park, and that a review was already planned for the new year. Traders say they would settle for two hours and an end to the warden's habit of arriving at ten past nine.

units.title: Dellow Court tenants say stairwell lights fail every night
units.author: weypost
units.text: Residents of Dellow Court, the fourteen-storey block off Ferrier Road, say the stairwell lights between the sixth and eighth floors have failed every night for a week, leaving older tenants to feel their way down in the dark when the lift is out of service.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The residents' association said it reported the fault to the building's managers, Kerrow Estates, on the first night and several times since. 'It's a maintenance issue, which is still an issue,' its secretary said. 'People have to use those stairs, some of them twice a day with shopping.'

units.author: weypost
units.text: Kerrow Estates said it was aware of a reported lighting fault and that a contractor would attend in due course. Tenants say the lift has been out of order on three of the past seven days. A meeting of residents is planned for tomorrow evening in the block's community room.

units.title: Bus depot cleaners to vote on night pay offer
units.author: weypost
units.text: Cleaners at Weyhaven's main bus depot will vote next week on a revised offer for night work, after rejecting a flat-rate rise in the summer. The new offer adds a premium for shifts starting after midnight and paid breaks for the first time.

units.author: weypost
units.text: One cleaner, who has worked nights at the depot for eleven years, said the money mattered less to her than the lighting in the yard. 'Half the lamps over the wash bays have been out since the summer. You clean a bus by torchlight and then they tell you you've missed a bit.'

units.title: Day-rate contracts: who carries the weather?
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: A fixed per-tree price with a daily labour allowance is common on large clearances, and it puts most of the weather risk on the contractor. Fog, storms and short daylight do not stop the clock. The Grieve Land Services contract on Kittering Holm, reported earlier this month, is a typical example at an unusual scale.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Legal advisers to the trade association recommend that contractors negotiate a lost-day clause covering weather that prevents safe felling. Few manage it. As one site manager put it to us this week: 'You sign the job you can get, and then you pray for wind from the right direction.'

units.title: Pay statement available: period 1
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Your pay statement for period 1 (contract days 1 to 7) is now available. Contract: Kittering Holm clearance. Day rate per worker: $300. Piece rate: $100 per tree, paid as timber is delivered. Statement reference: GLS-KH-0107. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address. Contact Operations with any queries.

units.title: Arrears notice: crew wages
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Our records show crew wages outstanding against your site account for the current period. Reference: GLS-KH-0108. Outstanding wages should be settled before the next statement date to avoid referral to Operations. If you believe this notice is in error, please contact Operations. This is an automated message. Please do not reply.

units.title: Leaver processed
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: A leaver has been processed against your site roster. Final pay will be calculated to the last day worked and issued with the next statement. Reference: GLS-KH-0109. No action is required from site unless the details are incorrect. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Week one check-in
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, just checking in at the end of the first week. A few things: Numbers: no pressure, just checking where we are on numbers so I can give head office something tidy. Fog: the Met Office says two more days. Please don't fell anything where you can't see the drop zone. Boat: still running, but expect it later than usual while this sits. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Fog week? We've got you covered!
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Fog week? We've got you covered! This week only, 20% off waterproof storage boxes, dry bags and our best-selling camp mats. Keep your kit dry and your spirits drier! (We mean higher. Our copywriter has been spoken to.) Free delivery to all mainland addresses and selected island landings.

units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Five ways to keep your camp cosy in damp weather! 1. Hang wet clothes high, never by the door. 2. A tin of rice keeps phones happy. 3. Crack a window: condensation is the enemy! 4. A lantern by the bunks makes everything feel warmer. 5. A hot drink before bed. You're welcome!

units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Customer of the week! A reader on Lisle sent us a photo of her allotment shed lit by three of our Beacon lanterns, glowing through the fog like a little lighthouse. Gorgeous! Send us your photos and you could win a lantern of your own. You can unsubscribe at any time using the link below.

units.title: Supply boat in the fog
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the skipper rang to say he is sailing from Gilliver at reduced speed while the fog holds, so the drop at the dock may be an hour or two later than you are used to. He will sound his horn off the island rather than come in blind. Nothing for you to do, except please nobody stand on the end of the dock in the murk. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Fwd: H&S note on restricted visibility
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, forwarding this from our H&S lead, sorry for the formality. Summary: no felling where the drop zone isn't fully visible; headlamps and hi-vis on at all times outside camp in fog; radios checked at the start of each shift; nobody works alone out of sight of the others. I know you know all this. Head office likes to see that I've sent it. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Crew wages
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, payroll has flagged that some crew wages are showing as outstanding on your side. I'm sure it's an admin hiccup with everything else going on, but crews notice these things quickly on a site like that. Could you get it settled before the next statement goes out? If there's a problem I can help with, tell me. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Week one: thanks
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, quick one: payroll ran cleanly for the first period, so thank you. That's rarer than it should be in week one, especially with a crew on an island and the post going by boat. Same again next week, please, and I'll stop sending you emails about it. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Emergency contact sheets
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, HR have asked me to remind every site lead that emergency contact sheets must be current for everyone on site. If anyone's details have changed, a phone number, an address, a new partner, let me know and I'll update the file. Some of ours are older than the crews. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Mist opportunity
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Chief, how's the fog out there? Here on the road job we've spent the week laying cones we can't see and then driving over them. Morale is cone-shaped. Courier says Grieve has you on that island for the whole month. Rather you than me, I get seasick in the bath. Hal

units.title: rehearsals, the dog, mum
units.author: sam
units.text: hi! quick-ish update. proper rehearsals for The Kingfisher and the King have started and Jamie practises Second Reed at the dinner table, so I now know the whole of act one including everybody else's parts. Pilot has decided the hall rug is his enemy and barks at it. mum's hip appointment got moved to next month, she says it's fine really. anyway, hope the island is nice, or at least dry. love, S x

units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: PS, one tip from the old days, since you won't ask for it. Keep the saw chains out of the damp at night or they rust by morning and you'll spend the first hour filing instead of cutting. Warmest corner you've got, even if it's under your bunk. Hal

units.title: Sorry to write again
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hi, sorry to bother you again. The weather on the news looks awful out there. Could you tell Tomas I'm fine and the car passed its test? He was worried about it before he left. And is he sleeping? He never sleeps properly when he's somewhere new. Sorry. Thank you. Ana

units.author: sam
units.text: forgot to say, the radio keeps going on about fog out your way. are the boats still getting to you? don't answer if you're busy, I know you can't really. I'll just keep writing and you can read it all in a heap at the end like a novel. a boring novel about a dog and a rug, starring Pilot. love, S x

units.title: Penhallow camp diary, 1894: November tallies
units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Nov. 12th 1894. Wind S.W. light, fog lifting by noon. Felled this day 61 trees on the north lines, 7 at the landing. Men in good heart. Wages pd. to Saturday: 14 men at 3s. 2d. per diem, less board. Cook complains of the damp in the flour. Lent Mr Dunmore my second pencil, which I do not expect to see again.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Nov. 15th. Rain all day. No felling. Men mending the sledge road and splitting shakes for the new hut. Tally to date 702. Hoskin cut his hand at the saw pit, dressed with brandy and linnen. He says the brandy did more good inside than out. The Lord giveth wet weather and taketh away the working day.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Nov. 19th. Fair & cold. Felled 74, a good day. Boat came from Gilliver with oats, salt pork, lamp oil 4 gal., and a letter for Teague which he would not read aloud. Men sang after supper. Mr Dunmore wishes the oil kept for the lamps & not used on boots, and has said so twice.

units.title: Carrow Point log, extracts (1904)
units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: 3 Feb 1904. Middle watch. 00:00 wind NE 3, visibility good, lamp burning well. 01:30 cleaned lantern glazing, salt crust heavy on the seaward panes. 02:40 steamer passing westward, lights correct. 04:00 relieved by Assistant Keeper Doran. Remarks: none.

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: 9 Feb 1904. Middle watch. Fog from 23:10. Fog signal started 23:14 and worked without fault 6 hrs 40 min. Coal for engine 3 cwt. Visibility under one cable. 03:20 a bell heard from a vessel at anchor, not seen. Remarks: Doran has a cough. Recommend he keep the engine room warm and his scarf on.

units.title: Miss Arnell's island notebook, 1923
units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: 14 May 1923. Lisle. Morning list: oystercatcher (many), ringed plover 4 pr., rock pipit, wheatear (male, fresh in), a single whimbrel on the rocks below the church. Thrift in flower on the north cliff. [Sketch: a pipit, unfinished, the subject having left.] Boatman for the Holm engaged for Monday at a price I shall not record.

units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: 16 May 1923. Gilliver. Fog until ten. The boatman says we may cross tomorrow if it lifts, and that he will land me at the old fish station but will not wait past the afternoon tide. I asked whether he meant the tide or something else. He said the tide. Eider in the harbour, thirty or more.

units.title: Amos Rendle's diary, 1934
units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Mar 3 1934. Fog. Did not go out. Mended the big net with Father in the shed, the tar is near done. Ling 4d a lb at Ammet they say. Tom says the curing station wants boys again for the spring. I was there at ten year old turning fish on the racks and it was a good place, salt and smoke and the women singing.

units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Mar 6 1934. Clear. Out at 5. Eleven baskets, poor. Lost a buoy on the Holm side where the tide sets hard by the point. Father would not go in for it so we left it. Mother lit the lamp for us at 4 as she always does, though we could see the harbour light plain from the mouth.

units.title: Gilliver fish-curing station (Kittering Holm)
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: The Gilliver fish-curing station operated on the south-east shore of Kittering Holm from about 1871 to 1938, salting and smoking ling, cod and herring for the mainland market. At its height it employed around forty people in season, many of them women and children from Gilliver who crossed daily by rowing boat (Society holdings, wage book GV/7).

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: The station is sometimes called a 'quarantine station' in later accounts. No record of any quarantine function has been found in Society holdings, the Courier archive or port health records [citation needed for the port health search]. The confusion may come from the station's isolation sheds, used to keep curing fish away from flies.

units.author: hist_wiki_pell
units.text: Talk note. The article should not imply that the 'isolation sheds' explain the quarantine story. That is a guess, and the wage book says nothing about sheds of any kind. I have marked it. Also, 'around forty people' comes from a single season, 1889; most seasons show half that. Please cite by season. Pell.

units.title: From the archive: the timber camp men come home (1895)
units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Editor's note. This item appeared in the Courier's Gilliver correspondence in early 1895 and is the paper's only contemporary mention of the timber camp's return. The correspondent was not named, and the Courier did not send anyone to the Holm. We reproduce it as printed, misprints included. G. Faulds, archive desk.

units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: The men of the Holm timber camp came ashore at Gilliver on Thursday last, rather before the season's end was looked for, and in poor spirits, for which the weather is no doubt to blame. Several were lodged at the Anchor until the Ammet carrier could take them on. Your correspondent understands the camp is to be closed for the winter and the tally is a respectable one. The Anchor reports a brisk week.

units.title: LB-0233: Brackwater Woods, dawn chorus (1988)
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-0233. Date: 24 April 1988. Location: Brackwater Woods, east ride near the reservoir fence. Kit: cassette portable, single dynamic mic in a sock. Duration: 46:10. Content: dawn chorus, wren and blackbird prominent; tawny owl until 04:58; a vehicle on the reservoir road at 05:20. Curator's note: the sock is mentioned on the tape box and accounts for the dull top end.
